core_territory: Eastern Paraguay between the Paraguay and Parana rivers
domain_territory: Misiones in Argentina; the Parana borderlands
sphere_territory: The Gran Chaco west of the Paraguay river; western Parana
anchor_cities: Asuncion; Encarnacion; Ciudad del Este; Posadas
founding_population: Guarani peoples under a Jesuit mission system, producing a bilingual society in which Guarani remained the majority spoken language
characteristic_institution: The Jesuit reduction - mission towns with communal production, expelled 1767
notes: THE STRONGEST CANDIDATE FOR A 14TH REGION. Paraguay does not fit the Platine Plain: it is Guarani-speaking, has a Jesuit-mission founding institution unlike anything else in the region, and Ribeiro classes it as a Povo Novo - the opposite tier from its neighbors. Jesuit reduction detail not independently verified.

core_territory: The dry forest plain west of the Paraguay river
domain_territory: Western Paraguay; southeastern Bolivia; the Argentine Chaco provinces
sphere_territory: The Bolivian Chaco fringe; the Santiago del Estero transition
founding_population: Guaycuru, Wichi, Ayoreo and other Indigenous peoples of the dry forest, never effectively colonized
characteristic_institution: None held - a zone of missions, cattle frontier and the Chaco War (1932-35), not a founding settlement
notes: A distinct dry-forest zone with its own Indigenous peoples and its own history of resisting colonization. Arguably deserves its own entry; folded into spheres here.

core_territory: The Choco department of Colombia and Esmeraldas province of Ecuador
domain_territory: The Colombian and Ecuadorian Pacific coastal rainforest
sphere_territory: The Cauca valley fringe; the Panamanian Darien
founding_population: Afro-descended populations, many from self-liberated communities, in a riverine rainforest environment
characteristic_institution: Riverine gold-panning and collective land titling - Colombia's Law 70 of 1993 recognized collective territories
notes: A genuinely distinct Afro-descended riverine society with collective land titles, folded into region 4's sphere on grounds of size alone. One of the wettest inhabited places on earth.

sphere_territory: Haitian diaspora communities across the Caribbean basin
founding_population: Enslaved Africans who overthrew the plantation and founded their own state - the only successful large-scale slave revolution in history
characteristic_institution: The plantation, then its violent abolition and replacement by a smallholder peasantry after 1804
notes: THE SHARPEST INTERNAL DISTINCTION IN THE SURVEY. Haiti is not the same object as Barbados: it is the one place where the enslaved population overthrew the system and founded a state. Four sub-splits of region 5 are defensible - Hispanic Caribbean, Anglo-Caribbean, Francophone Caribbean, and Haiti alone.

region_name: The Peruvian and Ecuadorian Coastal Strip
core_territory: The Pacific coastal desert valleys from Piura to Ica
domain_territory: The Ecuadorian coastal lowland; the Lima metropolitan zone
sphere_territory: The western Andean slope; the far northern Peruvian coast
founding_population: Creole and mestizo coastal society, with significant Afro-Peruvian and later Chinese and Japanese immigrant populations
characteristic_institution: Coastal irrigated plantation agriculture - sugar and cotton - plus the guano and fishmeal export economies
notes: Quite distinct from the sierra behind it - different economy, different demography, different politics. Folded into region 7's sphere here, but Lima alone holds roughly a third of Peru's population.

region_name: Primate Cities as Their Own Cultures
core_territory: Mexico City; Sao Paulo; Buenos Aires; Lima; Bogota
anchor_cities: Mexico City; Sao Paulo; Buenos Aires; Lima; Bogota
founding_population: Urban populations drawn from every region of their respective countries, forming something distinct from any of them
notes: A REAL OMISSION, FLAGGED. Each of these holds a population larger than most of the regions in the main list, and Woodard's own New Netherland precedent says a single dense commercial city can be its own nation. Not pursued in this survey. Would be drawn as points or small polygons, not territories.
